title: MLOps, Serving, Observability, and Technical Debt

content.value: Primary reading: Machine Learning Systems, Chapter 13. Supplemental: Google Cloud MLOps guidance, Hidden Technical Debt in ML Systems, and MLflow materials.

This unit studies how models become maintained services. Students learn model packaging, deployment strategies, feature consistency, CI/CD, model registries, experiment tracking, rollbacks, canaries, shadow deployments, monitoring, alerting, incident response, and ownership. Technical debt is treated as a system property: hidden dependencies, configuration sprawl, undeclared consumers, feedback loops, and glue code make ML systems harder to change. The goal is a service that can evolve safely under changing data and product requirements.
Supplemental sources for this unit are listed in the references below. Use them to compare the textbook framing with public talks, documentation, papers, and production guidance.
Studio: write an MLOps runbook for a model serving service. Deliverable: deployment path, monitoring dashboard fields, alert thresholds, rollback trigger, and incident checklist.

concepts.name: MLOps
concepts.description: Operational practices and tooling for reliably building, deploying, monitoring, and updating ML systems.

concepts.name: Model registry
concepts.description: A system for storing model versions, metadata, approvals, and deployment status.

concepts.name: CI/CD pipeline
concepts.description: Automated workflows for testing, integrating, delivering, or deploying code and artifacts.

concepts.name: Feature store
concepts.description: A system for defining, storing, serving, and reusing model features across training and inference.

concepts.name: Model serving
concepts.description: Running models in production so applications can request predictions or outputs.

concepts.name: Observability
concepts.description: The ability to understand system behavior from logs, metrics, traces, and other signals.

concepts.name: Data drift
concepts.description: A change in input data distribution over time that can affect model performance.

concepts.name: Technical debt
concepts.description: Accumulated design or implementation shortcuts that make future changes harder or riskier.
